extracted_content.title: PURPOSE
extracted_content.content: The purpose of this policy is to establish national drug code (NDC) billing requirements for all

extracted_content.title: PURPOSE
extracted_content.content: continuous glucose monitor (CGM) claims. Providers must include accurate NDCs on all CGM

extracted_content.title: PURPOSE
extracted_content.content: claims to ensure efficient processing and timely reimbursement. Missing NDCs can result in

extracted_content.title: APPLICABILITY
extracted_content.content: This policy applies to all Devoted Health plans.

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: This policy clarifies Devoted Health's classification of CGMs and their supplies, and diabetic

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: testing supplies, and outlines associated reimbursement requirements.

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: Per the Social Security Act §1861(s)(6), CGMs are covered under the DME benefit.1 In order for

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: a beneficiary's DME to be eligible for reimbursement, the reasonable and necessary

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: requirements specified in the related Local Coverage Determination (LCD)2 must be met as

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: well as additional payment policy requirements.

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: Devoted Health covers specific CGM brands (FreeStyle Libre, Dexcom, and Guardian) for

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: eligible members. FreeStyle Libre devices do not require prior authorization; however,

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: Dexcom and Guardian require prior authorization to validate medical necessity. As of January

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: 1, 2026, Freestyle Libre Devices and Dexcom will not require prior authorization. Guardian,

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: Eversense, and other CGMs will require prior authorization.

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: Devoted Health has preferred brands for blood glucometers and accompanying diabetic

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: testing supplies and applies preferred brand requirements to all diabetic supply claims.

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: Currently, both OneTouch and Accu-Chek are preferred brands. Effective January 1, 2026,

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: Accu-Chek will be the sole preferred brand. Beginning on this date, OneTouch and all other

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: non preferred brands will require an organization determination for coverage. Organization

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: determinations for non preferred brands will only be approved when there is a documented

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: medical reason the member cannot use the preferred brand.

extracted_content.title: HOW TO BILL YOUR CLAIMS
extracted_content.content: To ensure claims are can be accurately processed for payment, follow these billing guidelines:

extracted_content.title: HOW TO BILL YOUR CLAIMS
extracted_content.content: Providers are required to include NDC information on claims for reimbursement of all

extracted_content.title: HOW TO BILL YOUR CLAIMS
extracted_content.content: CGMs, CGM supplies, and diabetic testing supplies. The NDC must be an 11-digit

extracted_content.title: HOW TO BILL YOUR CLAIMS
extracted_content.content: number in a 5-4-2 format. If the NDC has fewer than 11 digits, leading zeros must be

extracted_content.title: HOW TO BILL YOUR CLAIMS
extracted_content.content: added. Examples are below; placeholders have been indicated with an asterisk:

extracted_content.title: HOW TO BILL YOUR CLAIMS
extracted_content.content: NDCs should be submitted in the normalized 11-digit format, with no dashes or

extracted_content.title: HOW TO BILL YOUR CLAIMS
extracted_content.content: spaces. Please preserve leading zeros. An example of the format is MMMMMDDDDPP :

extracted_content.title: HOW TO BILL YOUR CLAIMS
extracted_content.content: For a claim to be approved on the professional or facility submissions (CMS 1500/837P

extracted_content.title: HOW TO BILL YOUR CLAIMS
extracted_content.content: or UB-04/837I), the following NDC information must be included:

extracted_content.title: HOW TO BILL YOUR CLAIMS
extracted_content.content: ● NDC number: A valid 11-digit NDC in the required format.

extracted_content.title: HOW TO BILL YOUR CLAIMS
extracted_content.content: ● Example NDC: 0591-0933-01 should be sent as 00591093301.

extracted_content.title: HOW TO BILL YOUR CLAIMS
extracted_content.content: ● Unit of Measure (UOM): Such as milliliters (ML), grams (GR), units (UN).

extracted_content.title: HOW TO BILL YOUR CLAIMS
extracted_content.content: ● NDC quantity: The total quantity administered, including partial units (e.g., 1.5 ml).

extracted_content.title: HOW TO BILL YOUR CLAIMS
extracted_content.content: For more information on NDCs, refer to our NDC Billing Guidelines payment policy.

extracted_content.title: HOW TO BILL YOUR CLAIMS
extracted_content.content: Use appropriate CPT codes (e.g., A4238, A4239, E2103, A4253, A4256, E0607, etc.) on

extracted_content.title: HOW TO BILL YOUR CLAIMS
extracted_content.content: the CMS-1500, or X12 837P forms. Each claim line for these codes must include the

extracted_content.title: HOW TO BILL YOUR CLAIMS
extracted_content.content: Bill CGM supplies under supply allowance CPT codes (A4238, or A4239), which cover

extracted_content.title: HOW TO BILL YOUR CLAIMS
extracted_content.content: items such as sensors and transmitters. Supplies billed separately will be denied. Each

extracted_content.title: HOW TO BILL YOUR CLAIMS
extracted_content.content: claim line billed under A4238 or A4239 must include the corresponding product NDC

extracted_content.title: HOW TO BILL YOUR CLAIMS
extracted_content.content: for the specific sensor or transmitter supplied. Supplies billed without an NDC, or

extracted_content.title: HOW TO BILL YOUR CLAIMS
extracted_content.content: supplies billed separately outside the allowance, may be denied.

extracted_content.title: ACRONYMS AND DEFINITIONS
extracted_content.content: Continuous Glucose Monitor (CGM): Equipment that monitors glucose level on a continuous

extracted_content.title: ACRONYMS AND DEFINITIONS
extracted_content.content: Current Procedural Terminology (CPT): Set of medical codes used to report medical,

extracted_content.title: ACRONYMS AND DEFINITIONS
extracted_content.content: surgical, and diagnostic services and procedures.

extracted_content.title: ACRONYMS AND DEFINITIONS
extracted_content.content: Evidence of Coverage (EOC): Legal contract between a policyholder and health insurance

extracted_content.title: ACRONYMS AND DEFINITIONS
extracted_content.content: plan that details the plan's benefits and costs.

extracted_content.title: ACRONYMS AND DEFINITIONS
extracted_content.content: Durable Medical Equipment (DME): Equipment designed for repeated use, primarily for

extracted_content.title: ACRONYMS AND DEFINITIONS
extracted_content.content: medical purposes, not useful without illness or injury, and suitable for home use.

extracted_content.title: ACRONYMS AND DEFINITIONS
extracted_content.content: Local Coverage Determination (LCD): Decision made by Medicare about whether a specific

extracted_content.title: ACRONYMS AND DEFINITIONS
extracted_content.content: item or service is covered under Medicare, based on where the beneficiary lives and what is

extracted_content.title: ACRONYMS AND DEFINITIONS
extracted_content.content: National Drug Code (NDC): A unique, 11-digit, 3-segment number assigned to medication,

extracted_content.title: ACRONYMS AND DEFINITIONS
extracted_content.content: biological products and DME, serving as a universal product identifier.
